population.description: Adults with elevated triglycerides, at pharmacological doses (typically 4 g/day)

gradeRationale.note: Recorded specifically so the engine does NOT borrow this claim's Strong grade to justify a 300 mg/day general-wellness recommendation. Different dose, different population, different claim - see epa-dha-general-population-cv-prevention.

statement: EPA and DHA lower elevated triglycerides in a dose-dependent way, but the effect is established at pharmacological doses of around 4 g/day - a therapeutic use case, not an over-the-counter general-wellness one.

citations.title: Omega-3 Fatty Acids for the Management of Hypertriglyceridemia: A Science Advisory From the American Heart Association

doseResponse.summary: Meaningful triglyceride lowering requires roughly 4 g/day combined EPA+DHA, far above the 250-500 mg/day general-intake range.
